_README: config_language.json -- the DEFAULTS file for the LANGUAGE task, frozen at
T-L7.1. canonical_spec_language.json is the FROZEN CONTRACT; this file is what
an operator actually launches. The relationship is identical to
config.json <-> canonical_spec.json, and so is the rule: IF YOU CHANGE A VALUE
HERE, CHANGE canonical_spec_language.json IN THE SAME COMMIT, or the Gate 0
guard refuses every canonical_lang_b run -- which is the intended direction of
failure.
WHY A SEPARATE FILE RATHER THAN LANGUAGE VALUES IN config.json. config.json is
the defaults file the fifteen published arithmetic runs resolved through, and
config_hash is SHA-256 over the resolved config minus provenance and logging.
Editing config.json's training/model blocks to hold language numbers would move
the hash of every arithmetic run that re-resolves from it, so
runs/phaseB_MoRE_seed42__<hash8> would stop being the directory a re-run of that
config produces (see test_language_task_axis.py's module docstring). One file per
task keeps the two hashes independent by construction.
EVERY VALUE HERE IS EITHER MEASURED ON LANGUAGE OR DEFINITIONAL. None is
inherited-by-default from arithmetic without a frozen_by entry in the spec
saying so -- read canonical_spec_language.json:frozen_by before changing one.
The two that most invite a well-meaning edit:
batch_size 48 -- NOT 'as large as fits'. MoR (ffn_mult 24) is the memory-heavy
arm and sets the ceiling; at 64 it crosses 6 GB into the T-L7.0 soft-cliff
and its epoch time goes UP 1.03 h -> 2.31 h, costing the matrix 18 h.
epochs 3 -- a fixed BUDGET over ~135 M tokens/epoch, not convergence. All
three arms get the identical budget, which is what makes the comparison
valid; no arm is trained to convergence and the paper must say so.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT and must stay absent:
loss_weights.family_cls -- _apply_language_block forces it to 0.0 because the
family head reads h.detach() on language, so its gradient cannot reach the
trunk. Writing an explicit 0.5 here is REFUSED (a copied arithmetic config);
writing an explicit 0.0 would record a supervision term that does not exist.
Omission is the only correct state.
loss_weights.step_routing is present at 0.0 and that is FORCED, not chosen:
language has no per-token oracle expert to train a router against.
data.dataset_version / train_split_version -- stamped from the corpus manifest
by config.py:stamp_language_dataset_versions (T-L7.1a). A value written here
would be a declaration about bytes on disk rather than a measurement of them.
subset_fraction IS DECLARED UNDER `data`, NOT `training`, and the section is not
cosmetic. Every CONSUMER reads data.subset_fraction: engine.py builds the Subset
from it, run_context.py's proxy guard refuses a canonical claim on it, and
provenance publishes it as resolved_subset_fraction. It is also readable under
`training` for historical reasons, and load_config_defaults RECONCILES the two --
given in exactly one section it is mirrored into both, given in both and unequal
it RAISES. Placement here matches config.json, so a stray
`training.subset_fraction: 0.1` in a copied config is a hard ValueError at load
rather than a silently-honoured subset (the pre-T5.3 defect was a config saying
0.5 that trained on everything and reported 1.0).
